correctness.rationale: For exact 2x2 stable symmetric diagonal A and fixed PSD Q, the source-described constant-forcing IF-SSPRK2 stages algebraically collapse to Phi(X)=DXD+(h/2)(DQD+Q), D=exp(hA); each entry contracts by exp(-h(ai+aj)). Solving stationary equations gives (Xh)ij=(h/2)coth(h(ai+aj)/2) qij, versus continuous qij/(ai+aj), producing Langevin error kernel d_a,d_b,d_m. The Langevin function L(t)=coth t-1/t is positive and strictly concave: sinh^3(t)>t^3 cosh(t), established by differentiating a positive auxiliary log ratio; thus log L is strictly concave. For q11*q22>0, det(E)=q11*q22*d_m^2*(theta^2-r^2) makes strict PSD/singular/indefinite cases exact; rank-one r=1 and a!=b gives indefiniteness for every h>0 while both Xs are PSD. Taylor and large-h expansions yield the claimed negative eigenvalue limits. Independently checked 12 numerical instances of exact stationary error and determinant sign.

broader_coverage.reasoning: Zhang–Lan–Jing prove positivity preservation for differential Lyapunov equations under more general data, and Chen–Borzì cover exponential Riccati integrators. Neither positivity alone nor general finite-time convergence inequalities imply stationary matrix-order overestimation, since PSD iterates do not entail PSD error.
